headline: Getting a New York City public job takes months of screening. Firing someone past probation takes charges and a trial
dek: Flowcharts for five jobs, from the exam or license to permanent status, and from an allegation to a firing that sticks. Every box cites a statute, rule, exam notice, union contract or agency document; tap a number to see the exact language. Fired for cause means removal for misconduct or incompetence, not layoffs.
aiCaution:
Everything substantive, from the concept to which jobs and documents to use to the layout, was handled by the author, a human. The research and coding were done primarily by Anthropic's Claude and Claude Code under close direction.

The author insisted on quality control. Every verbatim quote was re-fetched from its source and machine-matched against the live text on Sept. 11, 2026. Links into the city's code library were opened and checked in a browser. City Charter quotes were cross-checked against a second copy of the Charter. Where documents conflicted, for example an exam notice and an older agency web page, the chart follows the controlling document and says so.

Nevertheless, the risks of using AI remain. Laws, rules and contracts change, and this is not legal advice. We would be especially grateful to hear about any red flags you notice.

entry.text: Free computer-based civil service exam, ranked list, then NYPD screening

entry.text: State teaching certificate, one TeachNYC application and a principal's offer; no civil service exam

probation.text: 4 years (the union says four years and a day)

probfire.text: Discontinued without a hearing; written reasons on request; advisory review only

hearing.text: One hearing officer under Education Law §3020-a, assigned jointly by the city and the union

entry.text: $47 civil service exam, ranked list, agency picks from the top three; or a provisional hire with no exam

firing.title: Only the police commissioner can fire a tenured officer, and only after charges and a department trial

hiring.title: A correction officer passes an exam and five screening gates, then serves a 24-month probation
hiring.subtitle: From the civil service exam to permanent status, per exam notice No. 6303 and Department of Correction hiring materials.

firing.title: A permanent correction officer can be fired only after written charges, a trial before a city judge and the commissioner's decision

hiring.title: A teacher needs a state certificate, city clearance and a principal's offer, then serves four years of probation
hiring.subtitle: There is no civil service exam. The state licenses teachers; the city school system and its principals hire them.

firing.title: A tenured teacher can be fired only after a hearing, and the hearing officer, not the chancellor, decides
firing.subtitle: A probationary teacher can be let go without one. The separate removal track for teachers rated ineffective was repealed in June 2024.

hiring.title: A clerical associate is ranked on an exam list that can last four years, then serves a year of probation
hiring.subtitle: Clerical associate is the District Council 37 title used here, per exam notice No. 5977 and city personnel rules. Agencies can also hire provisionally, without an exam.

firing.title: A permanent clerical associate can be fired through a state hearing or a union arbitration, chosen after a first conference
firing.subtitle: Probationers can be let go by notice. Provisional employees have far less protection.
